long_biography.plain_text:
George Callendine Heck was a son of Jonathan McGee Heck, a prominent North Carolina developer with interests spanning manufacturing, railways and banking. George attended Wake Forest and then studied law at the University of North Carolina. He initially practised with Pace, Holding & Heck in Raleigh and served as secretary of Interstate Trust Company.

By the early twentieth century he had established himself in New York. Later historical accounts describe him as a partner in a Wall Street investment house, while social registers place the family at Garden City and Glen Head. He married twice, first to Eugenia Morehead Gray and later Helen Brooke, and the family genealogy records three children across those marriages.
